scoreNote: This is NOT a claim that r5 is worse than r4. On every clipping metric r5 is materially better and I say so below. The brief's rule is explicit: if the blind call is instant, the score is under 60 no matter how much it improved. The blind call is still instant and sub-second. r4's 60 sat on that ceiling; 59 is me applying the ceiling as written rather than rewarding movement. The score does not move again by tuning value and hue — it moves when the pith collar stops being a drawn ring.
biggestGap: The pith collar is a drawn ring, not a lit shell: around the near half's cut face it is the same width and the same brightness at EVERY angle — 12-sector luminance 93,108,107,118,108,113,104,106,125,123,122,96, a max/min of 1.35 on the identical ungated geometric-band probe that read 3.95 on the same frame in round 4 and 2.77 on plate-02's lemon — because `capKey()` (species.js:462-464) dots `normalWorldGeometry`, which on the flat/domed cap disc the pith band actually lives on is constant all the way round the ring.

headline_probe_reproduction_and_honesty_.reproduction_offset_DISCLOSED: My rebuild of the gated probe reads systematically ~1.24x LOWER than my predecessor's on the SAME files: r3/05 mine 66.7% vs their 71.6%; r4/05 mine 56.3% vs their 69.6%; r4/04 mine 51.5% vs their 60.4%; r4/08 mine 57.9% on a 19px population vs their 73.9%. Those are not the same surface and there is no reason they should share a number. I reproduced the reference probe exactly: plate-02 near lemon half, annulus 3-22px inside the silhouette, 12 sectors: [125,120,129,166,166,129,60,63,79,78,85,94], ratio 2.77 (8 sectors 2.77), clip 0.00%, maxR 227 — so their reference reading is sound, it is just a reading of the wrong surface for this axis.
why_the_predecessors_1.8_TARGET_WAS_THE_.apples_to_apples_version_of_that_probe_o: Same silhouette-annulus probe, normalised to fruit radius (0.018-0.13 of diameter), run on our own near half: r3/05 ratio12 11.06 clip 11.99% | r4/05 5.26 / 9.88% | r5/05 11.77 / 3.74%. Our SILHOUETTE swing is not too small, it is 1.5-4x too LARGE (reference 2.77) because our unlit peel falls to L=11-26 where the reference's sits at 60-63. That is a deliberate consequence of R1's hard key over a black void and I do not score it against us.
why_the_predecessors_1.8_TARGET_WAS_THE_.the_probe_that_actually_answers_this_axi: The predecessor's own UNGATED geometric band — 1..6px outside the filled flesh-face mask, inside the fruit silhouette, excluding peel, no brightness gate — restricted to ONE half so the two halves' orientations cannot masquerade as a gradient. My rebuild reproduces theirs closely on r4/05 (mine 44,43,42,45,41,43,109,164,143,144,150,95; theirs 39,43,52,35,39,40 / 96,154,147,142,153,138 — same shape, same ~3.5-4x swing). the_gap_measured.builder_prediction_falsified_in_the_ship: rounds/reports/r5-fruit-mat.md section C predicts the band 'runs display luminance 49 -> 149 around a camera-facing cap (max/min 3.02)' once cutter.js's collar tilt is included, and capKey's own docstring at species.js:451 claims 1.545x composing with 'the collar normal's own 3.6x of E-swing'. Shipped frame: 1.35x, and the band runs 93->125, not 49->149. Same failure mode as round 4 — a rig prediction, not an output measurement.
the_gap_measured.the_mechanism_in_the_source: species.js:462-464 `capKey(amb, gain) = saturate(dot(normalWorldGeometry, KEY_DIR)).mul(gain).add(amb)`. `normalWorldGeometry` is the GEOMETRIC normal. The pith band is not on cutter.js's chamfer collar — it is mixed into the FLESH material's colorNode (species.js:1391, `alb.assign(mix(alb, pithC, L.pith))`) by `wmLayers(cc)` off the radial cap parameter, i.e. it lies on the cap disc. A cap disc's geometric normal is constant azimuthally (a dome varies with radius, not with angle), so capKey returns the SAME scalar at every point of the ring. The 3.6x collar swing the comment relies on lives on a different material on a different surface and never reaches the pith. The residual 1.35x is whatever leaks through from the relief bump in normalNode, which capKey does not read.
the_gap_measured.what_a_lit_collar_should_do: The key is 60.7deg off the camera axis, so a camera-facing cap sits at N.L = cos(60.7) = 0.489. Tilt a collar +-20deg about that in the plane containing the key and N.L runs cos(40.7)=0.758 to cos(80.7)=0.161 — a diffuse swing of 4.7x. The file's own comment says 3.6x. Measured: 1.35x. Nothing in the render is doing this.

evidence.blind_call: Instant, sub-second, on /tmp/blind.png (plate-01's melon left, our r5/05 near half right, matched to the same pixel size). What names it is the collar: a bright cream-grey annulus of near-constant width running the entire 360deg of the cut face at near-constant brightness, with a hard outer edge against the rind, brighter than anything else on the fruit. On plate-01 there is no ring — the pith is a wedge that only appears where the cut edge is oblique, thickens and thins by a factor of several around the arc, shades from cream to dark green as it turns out of the key, and dissolves into the flesh with no boundary at all. On 04-cut+250ms at 4x the same collar reads as a 1-2px stroked outline that continues around the un-cut silhouette of the rind, which is what an outline in a vector drawing looks like. Everything else on this axis is now arguable on the numbers; that ring is not.

fix: One change, in src/fruit/species.js, and do not touch stage.js or the albedos again. `capKey()` at species.js:462-464 dots `normalWorldGeometry`, which is azimuthally CONSTANT on the cap disc where the pith band is actually mixed in (species.js:1391 / :1635, `mix(alb, pithC, L.pith)` driven by `wmLayers(cc)`'s radial parameter). The 3.6x of collar E-swing the docstring at species.js:124-136 and :451-452 relies on belongs to cutter.js's chamfer wall, which is a different material on a different surface and never reaches the pith. Give capKey a normal that rotates around the ring: build the cap-plane radial direction in world space once (the cap tangent frame is already available where `rad`/`cc` are derived), tilt it by the layered zone's own profile slope, and dot THAT with KEY_DIR — `capKey(amb, gain, N = normalize(normalWorldGeometry + radialWorld * slope))`. Two extra ALU in colorNode, no new uniforms, no new programs. Slope should be the +-20deg the collar geometry already uses, which on a camera-facing cap gives N.L 0.161..0.758 and a diffuse swing of 4.7x before amb/gain. Then set amb/gain so the LIT spoke lands at plate-01's pith (200,159,113) and the unlit spoke at roughly a third of it, and take the opportunity to pull B down ~15% (our collar B/R is 0.644 against the plate's 0.55-0.58; it reads grey, not cream). ACCEPT ONLY WHEN, measured on the shipped frames with the ungated one-half geometric band (1..6px outside the filled flesh-face mask, inside the silhouette, excluding peel, 12 sectors, no brightness gate): 05-cut+500ms near half returns a max/min >= 3.0 (r5: 1.35, r4: 3.95) with all 12 sectors populated, AND clip R>=254 stays at or below the current 5.6% on that band and 4.2% on the whole body. Do not accept a rig prediction for this number; it has been wrong two rounds running.
